extracted.intended_audience: clinical researchers, methodologists, and clinicians conducting or evaluating reliability/validity studies of clinical measurement instruments
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and exemplars for designing, analysing, and reporting reliability and validity studies of clinical measurement tools (intrarater/interrater/test-retest reliability, agreement, measurement error, and diagnostic/predictive validity). Includes methods for abstracting unstructured EMR data and methodological appraisal of guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report intrarater and interrater reliability separately
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish and report both intrarater (repeatability by same rater) and interrater (agreement across different raters) reliability measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many studies compute both (e.g., ICCs for intrarater and interrater). Interpret differences (e.g., intrarater often higher than interrater) and use findings to recommend clinical practice (e.g., serial measures by same examiner).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use appropriate reliability statistics (ICC, kappa, weighted kappa, Fleiss' kappa)
rubrics_metrics.description: Select and report the reliability coefficient appropriate to the data type: intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) for continuous measures; Cohen's kappa, weighted kappa, or Fleiss' kappa for categorical/ordinal ratings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State which statistic was used and why; report model/type when relevant (e.g., ICC(2,1)); use weighted kappa for ordinal items and Fleiss' kappa for multiple raters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report measurement error metrics (SEM, SRD, MDC, CVME)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantify measurement error and smallest detectable/real change using standard error of measurement (SEM), smallest real difference (SRD), minimal detectable change (MDC), and coefficients of variation for method error (CVME).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculate MDC at a stated confidence level (e.g., 95%); present both absolute and percentage MDC where useful for clinical interpretation (e.g., BESTest MDC 7.6% / 8.2 points).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use agreement analyses (Bland-Altman plots) for score agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess agreement between two measurement methods or between raters using Bland-Altman plots and report limits of agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for total-score agreement (e.g., QoL-AD); report bias and limits and interpret whether agreement is clinically acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report diagnostic/predictive validity (sensitivity, specificity, ROC/AUC)
rubrics_metrics.description: For instruments intended to predict outcomes or classify conditions, report diagnostic performance using sensitivity, specificity, ROC curves and area under the curve (AUC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare candidate method against a reference standard and present 95% confidence intervals for these metrics (e.g., Braden(ALB) vs Braden scale; report AUCs and statistical comparisons).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide confidence intervals for reliability and validity estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Accompany point estimates (ICC, kappa, AUC, sensitivity/specificity) with 95% confidence intervals to show precision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CI reporting allows assessment of estimate precision and whether observed values meet predefined thresholds (examples throughout the abstracts show ICC and kappa with 95% CIs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Define and justify acceptable thresholds for reliability (e.g., kappa ≥ 0.60, ICC benchmarks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify what constitutes acceptable/good/excellent reliability for the study a priori (examples: acceptable kappa set to .60; PRECIS-2 considered acceptable with ICC >0.65).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State threshold rationale (clinical relevance or published benchmarks) and discuss domains/items that may be harder to rate (e.g., recruitment or flexibility domains in PRECIS-2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify and use an adequate number of repeated measurements
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine and report how many repeated measures are required to reach acceptable reliability for the metric under study (e.g., TrA thickness: two repeated measurements; TrA thickness change: at least three).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use empirical analysis (e.g., compare single vs mean of repeated measures) to justify required repeats to reach target ICCs or SEMs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess and report impact of rater training on reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether training affects interrater reliability and report pre- and post-training reliability where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some instruments show little change with training except for less-experienced raters (e.g., GRID-HAMD); report subgroup effects and rater experience levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use blinded independent raters and standardized rating procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ blinded raters and standardized assessment procedures (e.g., video-based ratings, pre-specified scoring guides) to reduce bias and increase reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blinding and standardization were used in many studies (e.g., EMG blinded interpretation, duplicate video ratings) and are recommended to improve validity of reliability estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use task-specific checklists and global rating scales for procedural assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: For procedural skill assessment, combine behaviourally-anchored task-specific checklists (CL) with additive or summative global rating scales (GRS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare recording vantage points or modalities (e.g., first-person vs third-person video) and report CL and GRS reliability and mean differences (use t-tests where appropriate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply a phase-based, fit-for-use approach for abstracting unstructured EMR data
rubrics_metrics.description: For unstructured data abstraction across sites, adopt a four-step approach: (1) team building, (2) identification of challenges, (3) adaptation of abstraction methods, (4) systematic data quality monitoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This more time-intensive, phase-based approach can markedly increase inter-rater reliability for unstructured elements (example achieved kappas ≥ 0.89).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use validated appraisal instruments for guideline methodological quality (AGREE II)
rubrics_metrics.description: When assessing methodological quality of guidelines, use validated tools (e.g., AGREE II) and report overall ratings (e.g., 7-point scale) and inter-rater agreement (weighted kappa).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow tool instructions, exclude guidelines that don't meet inclusion criteria, and report domain-level and overall scores with reliability statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report domain-level reliability for multi-domain tools (e.g., PRECIS-2)
rubrics_metrics.description: When using multi-domain tools, report reliability per domain as well as overall (e.g., PRECIS-2 nine domains with ICCs and discrimination ability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note domains that are difficult to rate and provide elaboration/guidance (PRECIS-2 had some domains with wide CIs and raters requested more information).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct and report criterion and construct validity analyses alongside reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate criterion validity (compare to reference standard) and construct validity (convergent/divergent correlations) in addition to reliability testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: CTS vs transgingival (criterion validity: sensitivity/specificity); suicide risk levels correlated with BDI-II Item 9 and affective disorders (construct validity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Perform duplicate analyses of images/data to assess analysis reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Include duplicate analysis (re-scoring of same images/data by blinded analysts) to quantify analytic reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duplicate image analyses can be highly reliable (e.g., TrA duplicate analysis ICCs 0.89–0.99) and help distinguish measurement from analysis error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider and report the influence of rater experience and context
rubrics_metrics.description: Stratify or report reliability by rater experience/clinical background and by patient subgroup or setting when relevant (experience affected SDLT kappa values; QoL-AD agreement varied by care setting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret differences and consider training or limiting raters to experienced personnel when sensitivity/specificity or clinical decisions depend on ratings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify ICC model and reporting conventions (e.g., ICC(2,1))
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting ICCs, state the ICC model and form used (two-way random effects, absolute agreement vs consistency, single vs average measures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BESTest and other studies explicitly reported ICC(2,1); specifying the model improves reproducibility and interpretation across studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report comparative reliability when evaluating alternative measurement methods
rubrics_metrics.description: When comparing measurement modalities (e.g., digital scanning vs neutral suspension casting; automated segmentation vs manual refinement), report ICCs and other reliability metrics for each method and compare measurement variability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight methods with reduced variability and better reliability across raters (digital scanning showed consistently higher ICCs than casting in one study).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide clinically interpretable thresholds for true change
rubrics_metrics.description: Translate measurement error/MDC into thresholds clinicians can use to judge whether observed changes are true (e.g., BESTest change of 7.6% or 8.2 points to be 95% confident of true change).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report both absolute point change and percentage change for ease of use across score ranges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set and report an acceptable kappa/ICC level a priori for categorical/ordinal items
rubrics_metrics.description: Define what constitutes acceptable agreement for categorical items before data collection (e.g., acceptable kappa level set to .60 in some studies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these predefined levels to interpret item-level agreement (e.g., QoL-AD item kappas below .20 indicate poor agreement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use appropriate statistical tests for comparing mean scores and visualization methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Use t-tests or other inferential tests for comparing mean scores across conditions or recording modes and present visualization where helpful (e.g., mean CL scores for 1P vs 3P video).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complement reliability statistics with mean comparisons to detect systematic differences between methods or raters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report sample size and composition used for reliability estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide N, subject characteristics, number of raters, number of repeated measures and interval between tests (e.g., test-retest 7–14 days), as these affect reliability estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include community-dwelling older adults N=70 with three testers; EMG videos interpreted three times one month apart. Reporting these details aids interpretation and replication.
